summary: Taylor Harris's September 15, 2023 article argues that sportsmanship is the foundation of amateur sports, shaping character, community and lifelong relationships beyond winning or losing. It uses anecdotes and quotes from coaches, players, a columnist and a teacher, and describes initiatives like the "Spirit of the Game" award and "Fair Play Fridays" that recognize and teach good sportsmanship.
one_line: Taylor Harris explores how sportsmanship builds character, community and lasting relationships in amateur sports, with local examples, quotes and recognition programs.
key_facts: Olivia Sanchez has coached the Westfield Wildcats soccer team since September 2023 and says good sportsmanship is the embodiment of teamwork and personal character.

On October 3, 2023, during a basketball game between the Riverview Raiders and the Eastside Eagles, Eagles guard Emily Li crossed the court to check on injured Raiders point guard Michael Thompson before medical staff arrived.
Emily Li said after the game, "It's bigger than basketball," noting that helping each other and showing respect is part of the game.
David Greene, veteran coach of the Lakewood Lancers volleyball team, said in a September 26, 2023 interview, "Our job goes beyond the court."
As of September 2023, the local sports council introduced the "Spirit of the Game" award, given quarterly to teams and individuals who exemplify outstanding sportsmanship.
Sarah Johnson, a local sports columnist, found in her October 19, 2023 column that award recipients felt a deep sense of pride that outweighed the joy of victory.
At a match between local rivals on November 12, 2023, applause for a player helping up an opponent lasted longer than any cheer for a goal.
Grace Matthews, a senior basketball player, said on December 1, 2023 that she made lifelong friends because everyone shared a commitment to playing the game the right way.
The "Fair Play Fridays" initiative in local schools started on September 30, 2023, with teachers and coaches highlighting instances of good sportsmanship.
Kevin O'Reilly, a physical education teacher involved in Fair Play Fridays, said, "We're not just teaching games; we're helping to form responsible, respectful, and principled individuals."
The article says the support of players, coaches, families and fans shapes the atmosphere that encourages sportsmanship.
The article concludes that how you play the game is the real triumph and that sportsmanship binds diverse groups into a cohesive community.
